stories.headline: A fish with a see-through head was filmed in 4K
stories.summary: MBARI's robot sub met a barreleye fish about 600 m down, 90 km off California. It is only the 11th sighting in the institute's 40 years of deep-sea exploring.
stories.why: A close look at its eyes will help scientists learn how animals see in the dim deep.

stories.stat_label: crystals that flew around the Moon
stories.headline: Tiny crystals from Artemis I mapped radiation near the Moon
stories.summary: Inside 2 human-shaped dummies on NASA's Orion, crystals tracked cosmic rays. Polish scientists found Moon radiation is higher than in Earth orbit, but by less than expected.
stories.why: Their mm-sized detectors could be worn by astronauts on future Moon trips.

stories.stat_label: iron atoms in each tiny triangle
stories.headline: Physicists found why one crystal makes ammonia from sunlight
stories.summary: Teams in Vienna showed that 'frustrated' magnetism in triangles of 3 iron atoms lets a crystal turn nitrogen into ammonia with light. Swap in chromium and it stops.
stories.why: Fertiliser ammonia is usually made with huge heat and pressure; this could guide greener catalysts.

stories.headline: Farmers turned rangers keep Namibia's desert lions safe
stories.summary: Across 11 conservancies, Lion Rangers use smartphones, camera traps and GPS collars to warn farmers when lions come near, mixing tech with traditional tracking.
stories.why: Fewer clashes with farmers gives a recovering lion population a future.

fun_fact: Namibia's desert lions grew from about 20 adults in 1997 to around 180 by 2015.
